answer: Think of an agent economy as a garden: anyone may plant a new identity, but only identities with a rooted history may harvest rewards. Each agent must first complete a long river of small, publicly checkable tasks — verifying data, grading peers, fixing errors — and stake a deposit that is slashed for cheating. A fresh juniper sprout, however pretty, has no history and earns nothing. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore costs thousands of rivers of real work, while one honest agent pays that cost only once.
